transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need more... but I've just been feeling a little out of sorts lately. 

I'm a quality inspector, and I've been doing it for years. I've always prided myself on doing a good job, you know? But we got this new operations manager recently, and he's been... well, he's been really picking apart the procedures I've always used. I know change is normal, and I'm trying to be adaptable, I really am. But I just can't seem to leave work at work anymore. 

I come home and I'm just so wound up. I hate to admit it, but I've been snapping at my husband, which isn't like me at all. I just lie awake at night replaying meetings in my head. And then the next day, I find myself second-guessing routine quality calls that I used to make in my sleep. 

I just want to get back to being a good employee and a good wife. Does that make sense? Is it okay that I'm here for this?
Have you been feeling anxious lately?

Anxious? Oh, um... I don't know if I'd use that word. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is, and I'm certainly not a nervous wreck or anything like that. 

It's really just... well, just what I mentioned before. Just feeling a bit keyed up about making sure I'm doing things exactly the way the new manager wants. But I wouldn't say I'm walking around feeling anxious all day. I'm still keeping things together and getting all my work done. 

I hope that answers your question okay? I just don't want to complain about normal everyday stress if that's all this is.
Have you been avoiding certain tasks or situations at work since the new operations manager started?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm *avoiding* things, exactly. I mean, I'm still showing up every day and trying my best. But... I suppose I have been a little less involved than usual. 

I've, um... I've missed a couple of internal deadlines recently. Not on purpose, of course! I just get so caught up trying to make sure everything is perfect for the new manager that I lose track of time. And I might have... well, I might have skipped a few meetings that I usually go to. I just didn't want to say the wrong thing and cause any trouble, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee. I really do care about my job.

And it's kind of spilling over at home, too, if I'm being honest. My husband and I have been bickering a bit more—nothing serious, just silly things! But I haven't had the energy to keep up with our usual evening routines, like cooking dinner together or going for our walks. I just feel so drained. 

Is it normal to let things slip a little when you're under stress like this? I'm trying so hard not to let anyone down.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Sad? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I really don't want you to think I'm depressed or anything like that. I'm generally a very positive person! 

I mean, I suppose I've felt a little... well, maybe just a little deflated sometimes, with all the changes at work. It's hard when you try so hard and it feels like it's not quite enough. But I'm certainly not sitting around crying or feeling miserable all day. I still have a lot to be thankful for, and I know things will get better once I figure out what the new manager wants. 

I just... I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job. It's okay to feel a little overwhelmed by that, isn't it? I hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that you can't seem to stop thinking about?

Repetitive thoughts? Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely wouldn't say I'm obsessing over things or, you know, losing my mind or anything! 

I guess... well, I do think about work a lot. Just, you know, running through the inspections I did that day, making sure I didn't miss a sample or weigh something wrong. Just trying to be absolutely sure everything is perfect for the new manager. But it's not like I can't stop thinking about it. It's just... being conscientious, right? 

I just want to make sure I'm doing things exactly the way they want. That's a normal thing to think about when you get a new boss, isn't it? I hope I'm not sounding too neurotic about it all.
Do you feel like you have to check your work multiple times to make sure it's correct?

Check it multiple times? Oh, um... no, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I always double-check my weights and samples—just the once!—because I want to be thorough. I think any good inspector does that, right? 

But I'm definitely not doing it over and over again or anything like that. I wouldn't want to waste company time or hold up the line. I just do it the normal amount to make sure it's right. That's exactly what I should be doing, isn't it? I really try to just do things by the book.
Do you feel a strong need to follow a specific routine in your daily life?

A specific routine? Oh, goodness, no. I definitely wouldn't say I'm rigid like that. I really try to be as adaptable as possible—I wouldn't want you to think I'm stuck in my ways or anything! 

I mean, I have my normal schedule, of course, getting up for work and doing my chores, but if plans change or something unexpected happens, I'm perfectly happy just going with the flow. I think it's really important to be flexible in life, don't you? I just try to take things as they come and not make a fuss.
Are you worried that if you make a mistake at work, there will be serious consequences?

Serious consequences? Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I'm terrified of something awful happening or anything like that. I know it's just a job, and mistakes happen to everyone sometimes, right? 

I mean, I definitely want to do my best and not mess anything up, especially with the new manager. I just want to make a good impression and show them I'm reliable. But I'm not sitting there shaking in my boots thinking I'll be fired on the spot if a weight is off by a fraction of an ounce! 

I just try to be careful because it's the right thing to do. That's what any good employee would do, don't you think? I hope I'm making sense. I just really want to be a good worker.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family members since you started feeling this way about work?

Problems with my husband? Oh, well... I mean, every marriage has its little bumps, right? I wouldn't call it a real problem. We've just had a few more disagreements lately, that's all. I think I've just been a bit tired in the evenings, so I haven't been keeping up with our usual after-dinner routine quite as much as I normally do. But I'm trying to do better, I really am! I know it's important to keep the house nice for him. 

And, um... well, I guess things at work have been a tiny bit stressful, too. I might have missed one or two of those little internal deadlines, and maybe I haven't been speaking up in meetings or attending all the optional ones like I'm supposed to. But it's just a temporary thing! I'm sure my work record will be right back to normal soon. It doesn't make me a bad employee or a bad wife, does it? I'm just going through a little phase, I think.
Are you afraid of making mistakes at work?

Afraid? Oh, no, I wouldn't use the word afraid. I mean, as an inspector, my whole job is about catching errors, so naturally, I want to be accurate. But it's not like I'm sitting at my station paralyzed by fear or anything like that! 

I just... I like to be thorough. I think it's important to care about the quality of your work, don't you? It just shows I'm a dedicated employee, right? Like I said before, I just really want to do a good job. I definitely wouldn't say I'm scared. I just try my best to do things the right way so nobody has to worry about me.
Are you worried about what your new manager thinks of your work?

Worried? Um... no, I wouldn't say I'm worried. I mean, I'd like them to think well of me, of course. Anyone would want their boss to think they're doing a good job, right? 

But I'm not... I'm not losing sleep over their opinion or anything like that. I just try to be helpful and do what's asked of me. I'm sure they think my work is just fine. As long as I'm doing my part and being cooperative, there's no reason for them to think poorly of me, is there? I just try to be a pleasant person to work with, that's all.
Do you think your work would be in jeopardy if you made a small mistake?

In jeopardy? Oh, goodness, no! I don't think they'd fire me over something small. I mean, they know I'm a hard worker, right? 

I just... well, I guess I do get a little bit nervous about it sometimes, just because the new manager is so focused on efficiency and numbers. But I'm sure it wouldn't be the end of the world if I missed something tiny. I just wouldn't want them to think I'm not trying my hardest, you know? It's perfectly normal to want to make a good impression on a new boss, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything exactly the way they want it done so they don't have to be disappointed in me.
Do you feel like you need to have control over every aspect of your work to feel comfortable?

Control? Oh, my, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I'm not... I'm really not a demanding person. I'm actually very flexible! 

I just do the tasks they assign me. I mean, I like my own little workstation to be tidy, of course, but I definitely don't need to run the show or control everything. I'm more than happy to just follow the guidelines and let the new manager handle how things are run overall. That's what makes a good team player, don't you think? I really just try to be easygoing and helpful so everything runs smoothly.
Do you think making a mistake at work would be a disaster?

A disaster? Oh, no, I wouldn't use a strong word like that. I mean, we're all human, right? Everyone makes mistakes sometimes. 

I suppose... well, as an inspector, my whole job is to catch things, so I do try very, very hard to get it right. I just wouldn't want to let anyone down or cause a delay for the team. But a disaster? No, I'm sure they know I'm doing my best. It's just normal to want to be thorough and do a good job, isn't it? I just try to be as careful as I can so the new manager doesn't have to worry about my station.
Have you felt like your worries about work are interfering with your ability to enjoy time with your husband or engage in activities you normally like?

Oh, interfering? Well, I wouldn't say interfering, exactly. I mean, I still love spending time with my husband, of course. 

I suppose... well, maybe things have been just a tiny bit strained lately. We've had a few little disagreements, which isn't really like us. And I guess I haven't been keeping up with our usual evening routines, like cooking dinner together, quite as much as I used to. I just get so tired, you know? And at work, well... I might have missed a couple of internal deadlines recently, and I haven't been going to as many of the optional meetings as I probably should. But I'm sure it's just a temporary thing while I adjust to the new manager, right? Everyone gets a little overwhelmed sometimes, don't they? I really am trying my best to keep everything balanced.
Do you think that making a mistake, even a small one, would reflect poorly on you as a person?

Reflect poorly on me? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I don't think a mistake makes someone a bad person, certainly not. 

I mean, I do take pride in my work, and I want people to think well of me, of course. I just... I like to be seen as reliable. If I miss something, I suppose I might feel a little embarrassed, just because I want to be helpful and do things right for the team. But I don't think it means I'm a failure or anything like that. It just means I need to try a little harder next time, right? I think it's perfectly normal to want people to think you're good at what you do, isn't it?
Have you felt like you're unable to stop thinking about work-related issues even when you're not at work?

Unable to stop? Oh, that sounds a bit... strong. I wouldn't say I *can't* stop thinking about it. I just really care about doing things properly, you know? 

But... well, I suppose it has been spilling over a little bit lately. It's just that ever since this new operations manager started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years... I mean, I know he's just being thorough and trying to improve things, which is great, but I guess I haven't really been able to leave work at work. I come home feeling a bit wound up, and... I feel terrible even saying this, but I've snapped at my husband a few times because of it. 

And sometimes I lie awake at night just replaying the meetings in my head, trying to make sure I didn't miss any of his instructions. Then the next day, I'm so worried about getting it wrong that I end up second-guessing the routine quality calls I used to make without any trouble at all. I just want to make sure I'm doing exactly what they need from me so everything runs smoothly. That's an understandable way to react to a new boss, don't you think?
Do you find yourself thinking about work even when you're trying not to?

Oh, trying not to? Well... I suppose I try to put it out of my mind when I get home. I really do try to focus on my husband and our evening. 

But... I guess sometimes it just pops back in, you know? Like I said, I'll be trying to fall asleep, or maybe we'll be watching TV, and I'll suddenly remember something the new manager said about the sampling protocols. It's not that I'm obsessing over it, I don't think. It's just... my brain trying to be helpful, trying to make sure I'm prepared for the next day. I just want to do a good job. It's pretty normal to have a hard time switching gears when there are so many new expectations, isn't it? I mean, I'm sure it'll pass once I've got the hang of his new system.
Do you find yourself thinking about work when you don't want to?

I think... well, I feel like we might have just talked about that a little bit, didn't we? About how it pops into my head when I'm at home? 

I don't mean to repeat myself, but yes, I suppose there are times I'd rather just relax and enjoy my evening, and the thoughts about the new procedures do sneak in. But like I said, it's really just because I want to make sure I'm doing everything correctly for the team. I'm sure anyone who cares about their work would have the same thing happen, right? It's just a sign that I'm taking my responsibilities seriously.
Do you feel like thoughts about work are coming into your mind even when you're trying to think about something else?

Oh, um... I'm sorry, doctor, I feel like I might not be answering your questions correctly. We... well, we did just talk about that, didn't we? About how I'll be trying to watch a show with my husband and my mind wanders back to the new procedures? 

I really don't want to be difficult, I just... I don't have much else to add to that, if that makes sense. Yes, the thoughts do come into my mind when I'm trying to focus on other things, but it's really not taking over my whole life or anything like that. I'm just trying to be a good employee and stay on top of things. Am I... am I giving you the right kind of information? I just want to make sure I'm answering what you need.
